source.author: Jan Treur
source.title: Temporal Factorisation: A Unifying Principle for Dynamics of the World and of Mental States

licensed_support: The paper independently articulates temporal factorisation in which past-pattern to future-pattern dependence can be represented through a mediating present-state property and applies the principle to cognitive dynamics. This supports the scientific intelligibility of abstracting across explicit-history and state-mediated temporal description.
exclusions: It does not establish equivalence of persistence and history-window structure in the Botvinick and Tulving sources.
It does not establish CPCG as uniquely correct or representation-neutral.
It does not itself support a cognitive-capacity identity verdict.
